fact_check.claim: Cost of Attendance minus Expected Family Contribution equals demonstrated financial need
fact_check.note: FAQ: 'Cost of Attendance – Expected Family Contribution = Demonstrated Financial Need'.

fact_check.claim: FAQ says EFC usually stays the same unless family reports a major change, 'and aid then shifts with your costs'
fact_check.note: FAQ says 'Your Expected Family Contribution remains consistent unless your family reports significant changes'. The second half (aid shifts with cost of attendance) is not attributed to the FAQ in what the page says; it is the writer's inference presented inside a linked quote.

fact_check.claim: Outside scholarships reduce self-help aid (loans or work-study) dollar for dollar; Cornell may need to reduce federal, state or other grants; upload award notice to Secure Document Upload portal
fact_check.note: FAQ: 'typically reduce self-help aid (student loans or work-study) dollar-for-dollar'; 'may be required to reduce federal, state, or other grants'; Secure Document Upload portal. The words 'until none remains' were not seen on the page.

fact_check.claim: Standard Student Contribution earned and saved over summer; if you cannot, request a loan via the Undergraduate Student Appeal Form
fact_check.note: Matches the FAQ.

fact_check.claim: Continuing U.S. students must complete the CSS Profile to renew the Cornell Aid Offer, and the FAFSA
fact_check.note: Page: all returning U.S. students must complete the CSS Profile; all U.S. students must also file the FAFSA.

fact_check.claim: Divorced or separated parents: both biological or adoptive parents complete separate profiles
fact_check.note: Page says both parents are required to complete separate CSS Profile applications.

fact_check.claim: 2027-28 CSS Profile as soon as possible after October 1, 2026 and no later than February 2, 2027; FAFSA as soon as possible after October 1, 2026
fact_check.note: Exact dates match.

fact_check.claim: Page does not say what a late filing costs
fact_check.note: Confirmed: no late penalty stated.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's page says to avoid uploading documents that have not been requested
fact_check.note: Page: 'Avoid uploading documents that have not been requested'.

fact_check.claim: Pell Grant rules for 2026-27 differ from last year's
fact_check.note: The page says the maximum Pell 'remains $7,395' for 2026-27. The article's framing that the rules differ from last year is not supported for the maximum, and the page as read does not say the SAI or other-grants limits are new this year.

fact_check.claim: Maximum Pell $7,395 for 2026-27
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: SAI of $14,790 or more (twice the maximum Pell) is ineligible; non-federal grants and scholarships at or above total cost of attendance are ineligible
fact_check.note: Both limitations are on the page.

fact_check.claim: If Pell eligibility changes, the Cornell Grant adjusts automatically; Cornell Grant-eligible students are not affected
fact_check.note: Page: Cornell Grant 'will be adjusted automatically to compensate for the difference'. The 'not affected' wording was not separately returned by the fetch; the adjustment statement supports the point.

fact_check.claim: Parent PLUS limits $20,000 per year and $65,000 lifetime per student, starting July 1, 2026; undergraduate loan limits unchanged
fact_check.note: Page: $20,000 annual, $65,000 total per student; most changes effective July 1, 2026; subsidized and unsubsidized limits stay the same.

fact_check.claim: Household drops when a sibling graduates / sibling left college
fact_check.note: Hard claim with no source. The Sun article is about the FAFSA no longer boosting eligibility for siblings in college; it does not say aid drops when a sibling graduates, and does not address Cornell's CSS Profile methodology.

fact_check.claim: Redesigned FAFSA, which replaced EFC with the Student Aid Index, no longer gives families extra eligibility with more than one child in college (Sun, January 2024)
fact_check.note: Article says the revised FAFSA 'no longer increases students' eligible financial aid if they have siblings in college'. Dated Jan 25/26, 2024. The EFC-to-SAI rename is not in the extract but is a well-known fact.

fact_check.claim: Kevin Jensen, executive director of Cornell's Office of Financial Aid and Student Employment, said Cornell meets 100 percent of demonstrated need and Cornell grant aid would increase if federal grant aid fell
fact_check.note: Title confirmed; Jensen quoted that Cornell grant aid will be increased to compensate. The 100 percent statement is from Cornell's administration in the piece. This is a 2024 student-newspaper source, acceptable here only as attributed context.

fact_check.claim: Missing paperwork is one of the nine reasons upperclassmen lose aid on uAspire's list; upperclassmen may have to file several forms with different due dates
fact_check.note: The page does not present a list of nine reasons. It does discuss forgotten filing deadlines and a counselor saying some upperclassmen fill out five forms with different deadlines. Remove 'nine'.

fact_check.claim: uAspire describes schools that front-load awards but does not name Cornell
fact_check.note: Article says schools, especially financially troubled ones, front-load merit aid then lower it; Cornell not named.

fact_check.claim: SAP evaluated annually after final grades post
fact_check.note: Evaluations completed at end of each academic year after final grades.

fact_check.claim: Undergraduate SAP: 67% completion, 2.0 cumulative GPA, 150% max timeframe (180 attempted credits for 120-credit degree)
fact_check.note: All three match.

fact_check.claim: Attempted credits include withdrawals, failures, incompletes and repeated courses; failing SAP means loss of eligibility with written notification; paying or sitting out does not restore; approved appeal gives one semester of probation
fact_check.note: All match the page.

fact_check.claim: Aid office phone 607-255-5145, finaid@cornell.edu, online counselor appointments
fact_check.note: Phone, email and Schedule Counselor Appointments link all on page. Phone and virtual appointment hours (Mon-Fri 10-1 and 2-4) are also listed and could be added.

fact_check.claim: Special circumstances appeal asks for an adjustment based on changes since applying or unusual family situations; needs documentation; decided case by case
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Appeals: typical response 10 to 15 business days, reviewed in order received, approved appeals may not result in additional grant aid, no merit aid, does not negotiate
fact_check.note: All quotes match.

beats_top.query: cornell financial aid decreased why aid offer lower than last year
beats_top.why: The Cornell FAQ (the top relevant result; the rest were old Cornell Sun pieces) explains the formula and outside scholarships but does not diagnose a lower offer. Our page does, with dated deadlines, SAP numbers and a questions-to-ask list, once the unsupported claims are fixed.
changes: Add a short line-item table near the top: letter line that dropped (grant, loan, work-study, cost of attendance, Pell) mapped to likely cause and the section to read.
Replace the unsourced sibling-graduation claim with what the sources actually support, and say plainly that Cornell does not publish how the CSS Profile treats siblings, so ask the office.
Add the aid office's phone and appointment hours from the special-circumstances page.

fixes: In Step 1 item 1, rewrite the sentence so the FAQ link only supports 'your Expected Family Contribution remains consistent unless your family reports significant changes' (https://www.finaid.cornell.edu/financial-aid-faq). Move 'if the cost goes up or down, your need and aid move with it' outside the link and label it as our reasoning from the need formula.

In 'Federal rules changed', delete 'Pell Grant rules for 2026-27 differ from last year's'. Cornell's page (https://finaid.cornell.edu/federal-financial-aid-changes) says the maximum Pell 'remains $7,395'. Say instead that the page lists these Pell limits for 2026-27 and that the Cornell Grant adjusts automatically if Pell changes.

In the sibling section, remove the unsourced sentence 'Households often see a drop when a sibling graduates' and retitle the heading to 'The FAFSA formula stopped crediting siblings in college'. Keep the Daily Sun finding (https://cornellsun.com/2024/01/26/new-fafsa-raises-concerns-for-students-with-siblings-in-college-complex-financial-situations/), and add one sentence saying the source covers the FAFSA only and Cornell's pages do not say how siblings affect the CSS Profile calculation, so ask the aid office.

In 'You missed a step or a deadline', change 'one of the nine reasons upperclassmen lose aid on uAspire's list' to 'one cause of lost upperclassman aid that uAspire describes' (https://www.uaspire.org/News-Events/Why-Upperclassmen-Lose-Financial-Aid); the page has no list of nine reasons.
In the outside scholarship paragraph, remove 'until none remains' (not on the FAQ page) or reword to 'dollar-for-dollar' only.
Add a diagnostic table after the opening paragraph with columns 'Line on your letter that dropped', 'Most likely cause', 'Section below'. Use only causes already sourced in the article.
In Step 2, add the aid office's phone and virtual appointment hours, Monday-Friday 10:00am-1:00pm and 2:00pm-4:00pm, from https://finaid.cornell.edu/special-circumstances.
In 'Common mistakes', change 'Waiting for a deadline pass' to 'Waiting until the February 2, 2027 CSS Profile deadline'.
